response.answer: Professional tier monthly uptime commitment: 99.90% (maximum allowed downtime of 43 minutes, 12 seconds per 30-day month). Enterprise tier monthly uptime commitment: 99.99% (maximum allowed downtime of 4 minutes, 19 seconds per 30-day month). citations.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments
citations.text:
### 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments

CloudScale measures service availability monthly across each calendar month. The uptime target represents the percentage of scheduled minutes during which covered services remain reachable, responsive, and error-free.

Table 1: Service Availability Commitments and Maximum Allowable Monthly Downtime

| Subscription Tier   | Monthly Uptime Target   | Max Allowed Downtime (30-day mo.)   | High- Availability Architecture       |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Starter             | 99.00%                  | 7 hours, 12 minutes (432.0 min)     | Shared cluster infrastructure         |
| Professional        | 99.90%                  | 43 minutes, 12 seconds (43.2 min)   | High- availability Multi-AZ clus- ter |
| Enterprise          | 99.99%                  | 4 minutes, 19 seconds (4.32 min)    | Multi-Region active-active failover   |

## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

output.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
output.text:
### 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy

Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware maintenance:

- Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
- Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between 01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
- Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
- Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident notice.

output.header_path: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

- Starter Tier: Self-service Knowledge Base, API documentation, and peer Community Forum (https: //forum.cloudscale.io).
- Professional Tier: Web Support Portal and email (support@cloudscale.io). Hours: Monday through Friday, 08:00 to 20:00 US Eastern Time, with 24/7 coverage exclusively for Severity 1 incidents.
- Enterprise Tier: 24/7/365 dedicated telephone hotline, synchronized Slack/Teams Connect channels, Priority Web Portal, and direct assignment to a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) with Tier-3 SRE escalation.

output.text:
### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

output.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
output.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
output.text:
### 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations

- Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the customer's monthly recurring fee for that month.
- Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card chargebacks.
- Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for downtime.

output.header_path: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
output.section: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
output.text:
## 6. Exclusions & Limitations

The following circumstances are expressly excluded from the calculation of Downtime and are not eligible for Service Credits:

1. Client Misconfigurations: Unavailability caused by client configuration errors, invalid custom code, improper database queries, customer firewall misconfigurations, or expired SSL/TLS certificates uploaded by the client.
2. Unauthorized Modifications: System disruptions resulting from customer actions that violate CloudScale documentation, unapproved administrative overrides, or unsupported third-party software installations.
3. Third-Party Internet & External Outages: Outages caused by external internet service providers (ISPs), public BGP routing disruptions, upstream transit carrier failures, or client telecommunication lines outside CloudScale's core data center edge.
4. Force Majeure Events: Unforeseeable events beyond CloudScale's reasonable control, including natural catastrophes (floods, earthquakes, severe storms), war, civil disturbance, national electrical grid failure, or government sanctions.
5. Beta & Pre-Release Services: Features, APIs, or products explicitly designated as "Beta", "Preview", "Experimental", or "Early Access", which are offered "as-is" without performance guarantees.
6. Resource Quota Violations & Rate Throttling: Service degradation or rejected requests resulting from customer traffic exceeding agreed contractual quotas or unthrottled client loops triggering automated rate limiters.
7. Properly Announced Scheduled Maintenance: Maintenance executed within designated windows adhering to the mandatory 48-hour advance notification requirement.
8. Account Suspensions: Outages caused by account suspension or termination due to overdue unpaid invoices or material violations of CloudScale's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

| Subscription Tier   | Monthly Uptime Target   | Max Allowed Downtime (30-day mo.)   | High- Availability Architecture       |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Starter             | 99.00%                  | 7 hours, 12 minutes (432.0 min)     | Shared cluster infrastructure         |
| Professional        | 99.90%                  | 43 minutes, 12 seconds (43.2 min)   | High- availability Multi-AZ clus- ter |
| Enterprise          | 99.99%                  | 4 minutes, 19 seconds (4.32 min)    | Multi-Region active-active failover   |

retrieved_document_chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
retrieved_document_chunks.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
retrieved_document_chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
retrieved_document_chunks.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

retrieved_document_chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
retrieved_document_chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
retrieved_document_chunks.text:
### 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy

Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware maintenance:

- Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
- Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between 01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
- Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
- Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident notice.

retrieved_document_chunks.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

retrieved_document_chunks.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
retrieved_document_chunks.text:
### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

retrieved_document_chunks.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
retrieved_document_chunks.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
retrieved_document_chunks.text:
### 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations

- Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the customer's monthly recurring fee for that month.
- Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card chargebacks.
- Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for downtime.

## 6. Exclusions & Limitations

The following circumstances are expressly excluded from the calculation of Downtime and are not eligible for Service Credits:

1. Client Misconfigurations: Unavailability caused by client configuration errors, invalid custom code, improper database queries, customer firewall misconfigurations, or expired SSL/TLS certificates uploaded by the client.
2. Unauthorized Modifications: System disruptions resulting from customer actions that violate CloudScale documentation, unapproved administrative overrides, or unsupported third-party software installations.
3. Third-Party Internet & External Outages: Outages caused by external internet service providers (ISPs), public BGP routing disruptions, upstream transit carrier failures, or client telecommunication lines outside CloudScale's core data center edge.
4. Force Majeure Events: Unforeseeable events beyond CloudScale's reasonable control, including natural catastrophes (floods, earthquakes, severe storms), war, civil disturbance, national electrical grid failure, or government sanctions.
5. Beta & Pre-Release Services: Features, APIs, or products explicitly designated as "Beta", "Preview", "Experimental", or "Early Access", which are offered "as-is" without performance guarantees.
6. Resource Quota Violations & Rate Throttling: Service degradation or rejected requests resulting from customer traffic exceeding agreed contractual quotas or unthrottled client loops triggering automated rate limiters.
7. Properly Announced Scheduled Maintenance: Maintenance executed within designated windows adhering to the mandatory 48-hour advance notification requirement.
8. Account Suspensions: Outages caused by account suspension or termination due to overdue unpaid invoices or material violations of CloudScale's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

input_chunks.text:
### 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy

Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware maintenance:

- Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
- Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between 01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
- Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.

input_chunks.header_path: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
input_chunks.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
input_chunks.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

input_chunks.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
input_chunks.text:
### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

input_chunks.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
input_chunks.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
input_chunks.text:
### 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations

- Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the customer's monthly recurring fee for that month.
- Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card chargebacks.
- Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for downtime.

chunks.text:
### 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments

CloudScale measures service availability monthly across each calendar month. The uptime target represents the percentage of scheduled minutes during which covered services remain reachable, responsive, and error-free.

Table 1: Service Availability Commitments and Maximum Allowable Monthly Downtime

| Subscription Tier   | Monthly Uptime Target   | Max Allowed Downtime (30-day mo.)   | High- Availability Architecture       |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|

| Professional        | 99.90%                  | 43 minutes, 12 seconds (43.2 min)   | High- availability Multi-AZ clus- ter |
| Enterprise          | 99.99%                  | 4 minutes, 19 seconds (4.32 min)    | Multi-Region active-active failover   |

chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

chunks.header_path: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
chunks.section: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
chunks.text:
## 6. Exclusions & Limitations

The following circumstances are expressly excluded from the calculation of Downtime and are not eligible for Service Credits:

1. Client Misconfigurations: Unavailability caused by client configuration errors, invalid custom code, improper database queries, customer firewall misconfigurations, or expired SSL/TLS certificates uploaded by the client.
2. Unauthorized Modifications: System disruptions resulting from customer actions that violate CloudScale documentation, unapproved administrative overrides, or unsupported third-party software installations.
3. Third-Party Internet & External Outages: Outages caused by external internet service providers (ISPs), public BGP routing disruptions, upstream transit carrier failures, or client telecommunication lines outside CloudScale's core data center edge.
4. Force Majeure Events: Unforeseeable events beyond CloudScale's reasonable control, including natural catastrophes (floods, earthquakes, severe storms), war, civil disturbance, national electrical grid failure, or government sanctions.
5. Beta & Pre-Release Services: Features, APIs, or products explicitly designated as "Beta", "Preview", "Experimental", or "Early Access", which are offered "as-is" without performance guarantees.
6. Resource Quota Violations & Rate Throttling: Service degradation or rejected requests resulting from customer traffic exceeding agreed contractual quotas or unthrottled client loops triggering automated rate limiters.
7. Properly Announced Scheduled Maintenance: Maintenance executed within designated windows adhering to the mandatory 48-hour advance notification requirement.
8. Account Suspensions: Outages caused by account suspension or termination due to overdue unpaid invoices or material violations of CloudScale's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

output.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

output.header_path: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
output.section: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
output.text:
## 6. Exclusions & Limitations

The following circumstances are expressly excluded from the calculation of Downtime and are not eligible for Service Credits:

1. Client Misconfigurations: Unavailability caused by client configuration errors, invalid custom code, improper database queries, customer firewall misconfigurations, or expired SSL/TLS certificates uploaded by the client.
2. Unauthorized Modifications: System disruptions resulting from customer actions that violate CloudScale documentation, unapproved administrative overrides, or unsupported third-party software installations.
3. Third-Party Internet & External Outages: Outages caused by external internet service providers (ISPs), public BGP routing disruptions, upstream transit carrier failures, or client telecommunication lines outside CloudScale's core data center edge.
4. Force Majeure Events: Unforeseeable events beyond CloudScale's reasonable control, including natural catastrophes (floods, earthquakes, severe storms), war, civil disturbance, national electrical grid failure, or government sanctions.
5. Beta & Pre-Release Services: Features, APIs, or products explicitly designated as "Beta", "Preview", "Experimental", or "Early Access", which are offered "as-is" without performance guarantees.
6. Resource Quota Violations & Rate Throttling: Service degradation or rejected requests resulting from customer traffic exceeding agreed contractual quotas or unthrottled client loops triggering automated rate limiters.
7. Properly Announced Scheduled Maintenance: Maintenance executed within designated windows adhering to the mandatory 48-hour advance notification requirement.
8. Account Suspensions: Outages caused by account suspension or termination due to overdue unpaid invoices or material violations of CloudScale's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments
output.text:
### 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments

CloudScale measures service availability monthly across each calendar month. The uptime target represents the percentage of scheduled minutes during which covered services remain reachable, responsive, and error-free.

Table 1: Service Availability Commitments and Maximum Allowable Monthly Downtime

| Subscription Tier   | Monthly Uptime Target   | Max Allowed Downtime (30-day mo.)   | High- Availability Architecture       |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Starter             | 99.00%                  | 7 hours, 12 minutes (432.0 min)     | Shared cluster infrastructure         |
| Professional        | 99.90%                  | 43 minutes, 12 seconds (43.2 min)   | High- availability Multi-AZ clus- ter |
| Enterprise          | 99.99%                  | 4 minutes, 19 seconds (4.32 min)    | Multi-Region active-active failover   |

output.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
output.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

output.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
output.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

output.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
output.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
output.text:
### 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy

Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware maintenance:

- Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
- Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between 01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
- Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
- Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident notice.

output.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.2 Response Time Matrix
output.text:
### 5.2 Response Time Matrix

Initial response time is defined as the duration between ticket creation and the first substantive technical response by a qualified CloudScale support engineer.

Table 3: Support Severity Levels and Guaranteed Initial Response Times

| Severity Level        | Operational Impact          | Starter Tier                 | Professional Tier            | Enterprise Tier               |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Severity 1 (Critical) | Total production out- age   | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 2 Hours (24/7/365)         | ≤ 30 Minutes (24/7 Dedicated) |
| Severity 2 (Major)    | Core features impaired      | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 6 Hours (Busi- ness Hours) | ≤ 2 Hours (24/7/365)          |
| Severity 3 (Minor)    | Non-critical defect / bug   | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 24 Hours (Busi- ness Days) | ≤ 12 Hours (24/5 Business)    |
| Severity 4 (Guidance) | General inquiry / re- quest | Community Sup- port (No SLA) | ≤ 48 Hours (Busi- ness Days) | ≤ 24 Hours (Busi- ness Days)  |

output.header_path: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions
output.text:
### 5.1 Incident Severity Definitions

CloudScale categorizes technical support incidents into four clearly defined severity categories:

- Severity 1 (Critical): Complete production outage, total loss of database services, or primary API failure affecting all end-users. No workaround exists. Critical business operations are completely halted.
- Severity 2 (Major): Core platform functionality is significantly degraded, API latency increases > 300% over baseline, or high-volume transactional flows are impaired. Limited workarounds exist, but throughput is degraded.
- Severity 3 (Minor): Non-critical software defects, localized errors affecting minor endpoints, or cosmetic portal bugs. Production systems remain operational without material impairment.
- Severity 4 (General Guidance): Administrative questions, setup guidance, documentation inquiries, or enhancement requests. Zero impact on production systems.

output.header_path: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.4 Support Access Channels by Subscription Tier
output.clause_title: 5.4 Support Access Channels by Subscription Tier
output.section: 5. Support Incident Severity Levels & Response Times / 5.4 Support Access Channels by Subscription Tier
output.text:
### 5.4 Support Access Channels by Subscription Tier

- Starter Tier: Self-service Knowledge Base, API documentation, and peer Community Forum (https: //forum.cloudscale.io).
- Professional Tier: Web Support Portal and email (support@cloudscale.io). Hours: Monday through Friday, 08:00 to 20:00 US Eastern Time, with 24/7 coverage exclusively for Severity 1 incidents.
- Enterprise Tier: 24/7/365 dedicated telephone hotline, synchronized Slack/Teams Connect channels, Priority Web Portal, and direct assignment to a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) with Tier-3 SRE escalation.

### 5.3 Ongoing Incident Communication Cadence

During an ongoing active incident, CloudScale provides regular progress updates until the issue is resolved:

- Severity 1 Incidents: Enterprise customers receive status updates every 30 minutes; Professional customers receive updates every 2 hours.
- Severity 2 Incidents: Enterprise customers receive status updates every 2 hours; Professional customers receive updates every 6 hours.

output.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
output.text:
### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

output.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
output.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
output.text:
### 4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations

- Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the customer's monthly recurring fee for that month.
- Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card chargebacks.
- Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for downtime.

### 3.1 Monthly Availability Commitments

CloudScale measures service availability monthly across each calendar month. The uptime target represents the percentage of scheduled minutes during which covered services remain reachable, responsive, and error-free.

Table 1: Service Availability Commitments and Maximum Allowable Monthly Downtime

| Subscription Tier   | Monthly Uptime Target   | Max Allowed Downtime (30-day mo.)   | High- Availability Architecture       |
|---------------------|-------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Starter             | 99.00%                  | 7 hours, 12 minutes (432.0 min)     | Shared cluster infrastructure         |
| Professional        | 99.90%                  | 43 minutes, 12 seconds (43.2 min)   | High- availability Multi-AZ clus- ter |
| Enterprise          | 99.99%                  | 4 minutes, 19 seconds (4.32 min)    | Multi-Region active-active failover   |

chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
chunks.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

chunks.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
chunks.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
chunks.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
chunks.text:
### 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy

Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware maintenance:

- Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
- Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between 01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
- Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
- Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident notice.

chunks.text:
### 5.4 Support Access Channels by Subscription Tier

- Starter Tier: Self-service Knowledge Base, API documentation, and peer Community Forum (https: //forum.cloudscale.io).
- Professional Tier: Web Support Portal and email (support@cloudscale.io). Hours: Monday through Friday, 08:00 to 20:00 US Eastern Time, with 24/7 coverage exclusively for Severity 1 incidents.
- Enterprise Tier: 24/7/365 dedicated telephone hotline, synchronized Slack/Teams Connect channels, Priority Web Portal, and direct assignment to a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) with Tier-3 SRE escalation.

chunks.header_path: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
chunks.section: 4. Service Credit Structure / 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion
chunks.text:
### 4.1 Eligibility Overview & Starter Exclusion

If CloudScale fails to meet its monthly uptime commitment, eligible customers may request a Service Credit. Service Credits represent a percentage discount credited against future monthly invoices.

Starter Tier Exclusion: The Starter tier is expressly excluded from receiving service credits. Starter tier customers receive 0% service credits under all circumstances.

chunks.header_path: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
chunks.section: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
chunks.text:
## 6. Exclusions & Limitations

The following circumstances are expressly excluded from the calculation of Downtime and are not eligible for Service Credits:

1. Client Misconfigurations: Unavailability caused by client configuration errors, invalid custom code, improper database queries, customer firewall misconfigurations, or expired SSL/TLS certificates uploaded by the client.
2. Unauthorized Modifications: System disruptions resulting from customer actions that violate CloudScale documentation, unapproved administrative overrides, or unsupported third-party software installations.
3. Third-Party Internet & External Outages: Outages caused by external internet service providers (ISPs), public BGP routing disruptions, upstream transit carrier failures, or client telecommunication lines outside CloudScale's core data center edge.
4. Force Majeure Events: Unforeseeable events beyond CloudScale's reasonable control, including natural catastrophes (floods, earthquakes, severe storms), war, civil disturbance, national electrical grid failure, or government sanctions.
5. Beta & Pre-Release Services: Features, APIs, or products explicitly designated as "Beta", "Preview", "Experimental", or "Early Access", which are offered "as-is" without performance guarantees.
6. Resource Quota Violations & Rate Throttling: Service degradation or rejected requests resulting from customer traffic exceeding agreed contractual quotas or unthrottled client loops triggering automated rate limiters.
7. Properly Announced Scheduled Maintenance: Maintenance executed within designated windows adhering to the mandatory 48-hour advance notification requirement.
8. Account Suspensions: Outages caused by account suspension or termination due to overdue unpaid invoices or material violations of CloudScale's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

input_chunks.clause_title: 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
input_chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
input_chunks.text:
### 3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60) seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

input_chunks.header_path: 2. Subscription Tiers
input_chunks.section: 2. Subscription Tiers
input_chunks.text:
## 2. Subscription Tiers

CloudScale offers three subscription tiers designed to match different workload maturity, scalability, and operational support requirements:

- Starter Tier: Created for individual developers, sandbox testing, and non-production proofs of concept. Services operate on shared multi-tenant cluster infrastructure. Support is self-service via community forums and public documentation. Starter tier accounts receive no uptime guarantees, have no response time SLAs, and are entirely excluded from service credit eligibility.
- Professional Tier: Engineered for growing commercial businesses, standard production web platforms, and operational SaaS workloads. Includes dedicated multi-availability zone (Multi-AZ) virtual compute resources, automated daily database snapshots, standard business-hours technical support, 24/7 on-call coverage for critical outages, and eligibility for financial service credits if availability targets are missed.
- Enterprise Tier: Architected for mission-critical enterprise systems requiring continuous availability, massive throughput, and stringent operational governance. Includes isolated single-tenant or multi-region architecture, continuous point-in-time database recovery (PITR with 1-second recovery point objective), a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), 24/7/365 priority hotline and Slack support, and our highest availability commitment of 99.99% uptime.

input_chunks.header_path: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
input_chunks.section: 3. Service Availability & Uptime Commitments / 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy
input_chunks.text:
### 3.3 Scheduled Maintenance Policy

Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware maintenance:

- Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
- Standard Window: Scheduled maintenance is conducted during off-peak hours on Sundays between 01:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC.
- Monthly Cap: Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed four (4) cumulative hours in any single calendar month. Any maintenance beyond 4 hours, or conducted without 48 hours notice, counts as Downtime.
- Emergency Maintenance: In critical situations (e.g., zero-day security vulnerabilities), CloudScale may conduct emergency maintenance with at least one (1) hour advance notice or immediate post-incident notice.

input_chunks.header_path: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
input_chunks.section: 6. Exclusions & Limitations
input_chunks.text:
## 6. Exclusions & Limitations

The following circumstances are expressly excluded from the calculation of Downtime and are not eligible for Service Credits:

1. Client Misconfigurations: Unavailability caused by client configuration errors, invalid custom code, improper database queries, customer firewall misconfigurations, or expired SSL/TLS certificates uploaded by the client.
2. Unauthorized Modifications: System disruptions resulting from customer actions that violate CloudScale documentation, unapproved administrative overrides, or unsupported third-party software installations.
3. Third-Party Internet & External Outages: Outages caused by external internet service providers (ISPs), public BGP routing disruptions, upstream transit carrier failures, or client telecommunication lines outside CloudScale's core data center edge.
4. Force Majeure Events: Unforeseeable events beyond CloudScale's reasonable control, including natural catastrophes (floods, earthquakes, severe storms), war, civil disturbance, national electrical grid failure, or government sanctions.
5. Beta & Pre-Release Services: Features, APIs, or products explicitly designated as "Beta", "Preview", "Experimental", or "Early Access", which are offered "as-is" without performance guarantees.
6. Resource Quota Violations & Rate Throttling: Service degradation or rejected requests resulting from customer traffic exceeding agreed contractual quotas or unthrottled client loops triggering automated rate limiters.
7. Properly Announced Scheduled Maintenance: Maintenance executed within designated windows adhering to the mandatory 48-hour advance notification requirement.
8. Account Suspensions: Outages caused by account suspension or termination due to overdue unpaid invoices or material violations of CloudScale's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:

$$\text{Monthly Uptime Percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month} - \text{Downtime Minutes}}{\text{Total Scheduled Minutes in Month}}\right) \times 100

Formula: Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Scheduled Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Scheduled Minutes in Month) * 100$$

Maintenance is required to apply security patches, upgrade operating systems, and perform hardware maintenance:

- Advance Notice Period: CloudScale will provide a mandatory minimum of forty-eight (48) hours advance written notice prior to any scheduled maintenance. Notice is published on the status portal (https://status.cloudscale.io) and emailed to account administrators.
